question: How do I hide search attribution? Is lunr_maxwords still recommended?
expected: show_attrib false; prefer maxwords; deprecated provider fields precedence; Algolia separatelogo.

result.answer:
To hide search attribution, set `show_attrib` to `false` within the `search` mapping in your configuration.

```yaml
search:
  show_attrib: false
```

Regarding `lunr_maxwords`, the documentation states that the legacy `lunr_maxwords` (along with `simplesearch_maxwords` and `fusejs_maxwords`) takes precedence over the shared `search.maxwords` setting.

Sources:
* [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)

question: I copied an old custom search page and now Fuse or Lunr says ChulapaSearch is not defined. What should I update? How do I keep FAB navigation working?
expected: v2.2.0: direct readable/minified Lunr and Fuse adapters require assets/js/chulapa_search.js before initialization, plus their provider library and generated store before the adapter. Standard search layout handles dependencies. Update local overrides together. Custom document shells should include components/scripts.html once for Bootstrap dependencies and chulapa_navigation.js for fab/dual; layouts inheriting minimal/search already handle it. No new YAML options. Link JavaScript assets and local overrides and complete demo sources.

result.answer:
The error occurs because the search page requires a specific layout and title to function with Chulapa's built-in search scripts. To fix this, ensure your page front matter uses `layout: search` and has a `title: Search`.

To keep the Floating Action Button (FAB) navigation working, ensure you are using a standard Chulapa layout (like `default` or `search`) that includes the necessary Bootstrap components. If you are using a custom shell, you must include `components/scripts.html` before the closing `</body>` tag to provide the required dependencies.

**Update your page front matter:**
```yaml
layout: search
title: Search
```

**Next steps:**
1. Verify the page uses the `search` layout.
2. Check that your `search.provider` is set to `fusejs` or `lunr` in `_config.yml`.
3. Inspect the rendered HTML to ensure the search scripts are loading.

Sources:
[Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)
[Accessibility and resource loading](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/06-accessibility-performance)

question: I want Fuse.js search at /find on my site under /my-blog. Is setting search.provider enough?
expected: No. Set search.provider: fusejs and search.landing_page: /find, and create or reuse one search page with layout: search and permalink: /find. Do not repeat /my-blog; theme adds baseurl. No account/API key/extra Jekyll plugin needed. Template already has Fuse.js, so avoid duplicate pages. Publish and test a known title; local index rebuilt during site build.

result.answer:
No, setting `search.provider` alone is not enough. You must also create a page with `layout: search`, a `title: Search`, and a `permalink` that matches your desired path.

To configure Fuse.js at `/my-blog/find`, use the following in your `_config.yml`:

```yaml
search:
  provider: fusejs
  landing_page: /my-blog/find
```

Additionally, ensure your search page is created with the correct front matter:

```yaml
layout: search
title: Search
permalink: /my-blog/find
```

Note that Fuse.js indexes only `posts` and `About` pages by default. If you use a custom navbar, you must also add the link to `navbar.nav`.

Sources:
[Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)

question: I set comments.provider to giscus but see no comments on my post. What else do I need?
expected: Use giscus.app setup with public repo, Discussions and app installed; generated embed belongs in _includes/custom/giscus.html (starter file is comment-only). Enable show_comments: true in post front matter with a supported layout such as default, keeping other fields. Publish and verify embed/thread, settings and blockers if absent. Existing repo/category/page mapping matters; no automatic migration of threads.

result.answer:
To enable Giscus comments, you must complete the following steps:

1.  **Configure the provider**: Ensure `_config.yml` is set correctly.
    ```yaml
    comments:
      provider: giscus
    ```
2.  **Embed the script**: Generate the embed code at https://giscus.app/ and paste the script/IDs into `_includes/custom/giscus.html`. Note that the file's existence alone is insufficient.
3.  **Enable on the post**: In your post's front matter, you must explicitly enable comments.
    ```yaml
    show_comments: true
    ```

**Important Restrictions:**
*   Giscus has no `website_id` configuration field (that is for Welcomments).
*   The page layout must be capable of displaying comments.
*   Providers do not migrate existing comment threads automatically.

**Next Step:**
Publish your changes and check the interface on the live article and your selected GitHub Discussions repository to verify the integration.

[Giscus comments guide](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/13-giscus-comments)
[Comments configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#comments)

question: How do I replace Fuse.js with Lunr search on my existing site?
expected: search.provider: lunr, preserve existing search options, reuse/create layout: search page with matching permalink and landing_page, no account/key/extra plugin, no duplicate output or repeated baseurl. Publish and verify a title/result; include_on_search false affects local index. Link /docs/34-lunr-search.

result.answer:
To replace Fuse.js with Lunr search on your existing site, follow these steps:

1.  **Update Configuration**: In your `_config.yml`, change the search provider.
    ```yaml
    search:
      provider: lunr
    ```
    [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)

2.  **Create/Update Search Page**: Ensure you have a page with `layout: search`, a `title: Search`, and a `permalink` that matches your `search.landing_page` setting (defaults to `/search`). The provider setting alone does not create this page.
    [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)

3.  **Verify Indexing**: Local Lunr indexes are built at build-time. If you need to exclude specific pages from the Lunr index, add `include_on_search: false` to those pages' front matter.
    [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)

**Next Step**: Restart your local Jekyll server after editing the configuration and verify the search page loads and returns results.

question: Can I enable Simple-Jekyll-Search without a hosted account?
expected: Yes: provider simplesearch, existing search mapping and matching layout search page. No provider account/API key/extra plugin. Publish builds index; verify result and clearing. Link /docs/35-simplesearch-search. Preserve settings and baseurl-safe paths.

result.answer:
Yes, you can use `simplesearch` without a hosted account. It builds the index at build-time and does not require an API or external service.

To enable it, set the provider in your `_config.yml`:

```yaml
search:
  provider: simplesearch
```

Note that `simplesearch` (along with Lunr and Fusejs) builds indexes locally. To exclude specific pages from this local index, add `include_on_search: false` to the document's front matter.

For a complete setup, you must also create or reuse a page with `layout: search`, a `title: Search`, and a `permalink` that matches your `search.landing_page` setting (which defaults to `/search`).

Sources:
- [Configuring site search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)
- [Fusejs search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/12-fusejs-search)
- [Simple-Jekyll-Search](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/35-simplesearch-search)

question: I have a Google Custom Search engine. Will a Jekyll rebuild upload my new articles to Google?
expected: No index upload to Google. Set search.provider google and top-level google_cse_id from existing engine, reuse/create matching search page; engine scope and Google indexing govern results. Local include_on_search exclusion does not control Google crawler. Link /docs/36-google-search.

result.answer:
No, a Jekyll rebuild does not upload articles to Google. Google Custom Search uses external indexing, meaning build or local exclusions in your configuration do not control Google indexing.

To manage visibility, you can use `robots: "noindex, follow"` in your page front matter to let crawlers read the instruction, but the page remains public.

[Search visibility](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/65-search-visibility)

question: I configured Algolia in YAML but have no results. How do I upload the index and exclude a page?
expected: Browser configuration does not upload index or create search page. Need application_id/index_name/public search_only_api_key plus matching layout search page. jekyll-algolia indexing plugin deprecated/unmaintained; dependency in plugin Gemfile group, bundle install. Use bundle exec jekyll algolia in the actual site folder or adapt the repository's .github/workflows/algolia-search.yml example (jekyll_src: docs); do not run both upload methods. Theme installation does not copy or enable the workflow. Separate ALGOLIA_API_KEY environment/Actions secret, never public config. Use algolia.files_to_exclude, not include_on_search false which sample uses for ranking. Check uploaded records and browser/index settings match. Link /docs/37-algolia-search.

result.answer:
To use Algolia, you must upload your index; theme installation does not enable uploads. For existing sites, you can use `bundle exec jekyll algolia` (ensuring `ALGOLIA_API_KEY` is set in your environment/Actions secrets) or adapt your `.github/workflows/algolia-search.yml`. Note that `jekyll-algolia` is deprecated/unmaintained; install it in your `Gemfile` under the `:jekyll_plugins` group.

To exclude a specific page from Algolia, add `algolia.files_to_exclude` to your existing `_config.yml`. This setting controls the uploaded index, whereas the `include_on_search` front matter flag only affects ranking.

**_config.yml**
```yaml
algolia:
  files_to_exclude:
    - path/to/your/file.md
```

**Next Steps:**
1. Upload the index via the command line or Actions.
2. Verify the live search results.

Sources:
- [Search engines configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#search-engines)
- [Algolia search setup](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/37-algolia-search)

question: Can I configure any Matrix homeserver for Cactus comments?
expected: No homeserver YAML field. Adapter uses Cactus-hosted service, registered cactus_shortname and provider cactus; enable show_comments true on default-layout post. Verify public article. Conditional Cactus resources only on comment-enabled pages is v2.2.0; do not claim improvement in v2.1.0. Link /docs/39-cactus-comments. v2.2.0 fixes conversation IDs; v2.1.0 requires local _includes/components/cactus.html correction using include.pageurl | url_encode | replace: underscore, percent5F (literal %5F), with no slash/underscore and distinct paths retained. Changing IDs may detach existing threads; record/verify mapping and provider migration before publishing. Fix absent from v2.1.0; local adapters override v2.2.0 files. Do not double-encode an existing override using the same mapping.

result.answer:
No. Cactus comments are hosted on Matrix only; there is no homeserver option.

[Cactus comments](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/39-cactus-comments)

question: Is a Welcomments website_id sufficient? Should I accept its generated templates?
expected: Needs provider welcomments, website_id, post show_comments true and external integration delivering _data/welcomments data. Review generated PR, retain customized theme templates; local files override theme. Publish and verify delivered data and rebuild, not only temporary browser placeholder. Check post slug matching old data; no automatic migration. Link /docs/40-welcomments-comments. v2.2.0 fixes form permalink to include baseurl. v2.1.0 project sites need customized local form with page.url | absolute_url | escape on hidden permalink; verify full public URL and review old overrides.

result.answer:
No, `comments.website_id` belongs ONLY to the Welcomments provider and is not sufficient on its own. You must also select `comments.provider: welcomments` in your `_config.yml` and set `show_comments: true` in your post/page front matter or `defaults.values`.

Regarding templates, you should keep the theme templates. You must deliver `_data/welcomments/` and rebuild your site.

**Next Step:** Verify your configuration and ensure the page layout is set to display comments.

[Welcomments comments](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/40-welcomments-comments)
[Comments configuration](https://dieghernan.github.io/chulapa/docs/02-config#comments)
